headers.comment: Each user's Gemini key sits in localStorage, where any script on this origin can read it - so the real protection is controlling which scripts can run at all. script-src allows only this site's own files and the Google script Firebase's sign-in popup needs; no inline script and no eval, which is what an injection would rely on. connect-src limits where data can be SENT, so even a script that got in could not post the key anywhere but Google. Styles allow 'unsafe-inline' because React and the charts set style attributes; a style cannot read storage. frame-ancestors 'none' is the clickjacking guard: a financial app framed inside another page can be overlaid so that a click lands on a control the user cannot see.
headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://apis.google.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com; img-src 'self' data: https://*.googleusercontent.com; connect-src 'self' https://*.googleapis.com https://apis.google.com; frame-src https://ai-expense-tracker-navya.firebaseapp.com https://accounts.google.com https://apis.google.com; manifest-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'

headers.comment: Stops a browser second-guessing a declared Content-Type, which is how a served file gets reinterpreted as script.
Never leak the path of a page in this app to a third party - a URL alone can disclose what someone was looking at.

Voice entry needs the microphone and receipt capture needs the camera, so both are allowed for this origin and denied to everything embedded. Everything else the app has no business asking for is switched off outright.
headers.value: microphone=(self), camera=(self), geolocation=(), payment=(), usb=(), interest-cohort=()
